hints.title: Parity Bitmask over Alphabet
hints.text: With only 10 letters (a through j), represent the parity of letter counts in a 10-bit integer mask.

hints.title: Running Prefix Parity Mask
hints.text: maintain running prefix parity mask where the i-th bit flips whenever character (a + i) is encountered.

hints.title: Querying 0 or 1 Bit Flips
hints.text: a substring has all even counts if prefix_mask[j] == prefix_mask[i], and exactly one odd count if prefix_mask[j] ^ prefix_mask[i] is a power of two.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def wonderfulSubstrings(self, word: str) -> int:
        counts = [0] * 1024
        counts[0] = 1
        mask = 0
        res = 0
        for ch in word:
            mask ^= 1 << (ord(ch) - ord('a'))
            res += counts[mask]
            for b in range(10):
                res += counts[mask ^ (1 << b)]
            counts[mask] += 1
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Maintains prefix parity mask frequencies over fixed 1024-element parity space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(N^2) substrings individually leads to time limit exceeded for N up to 100,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix parity bitmask runs in O(10 * N) = O(N) linear time using a fixed 1024-element frequency array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should map character parities to bitmasks and evaluate 11 mask variations (0 flips + 10 single-bit flips).
